<================================
Highly useful for advanced learning, specialized fields, and practical work!
The app version of the long-selling dictionary!

<================================

■ Dictionary Content Guide ■
・The Kenkyusha New Japanese-English Dictionary, 5th Edition, contains 480,000 entries with English translations, incorporating Japanese vocabulary from all fields, including specialized terms, slang, Japanese-made English expressions, place names, personal names, organization names, various titles, and Japanese cultural artifacts.

■ Enhance the dictionary content features with app functions! ■
・A compound word search function has been added as a dictionary-specific search condition.

・Scroll display of headwords! A "touch panel search" function has been added.

* In addition to bookmarking individual dictionary entries, you can also bookmark example sentences and other elements within entries individually.



■ Comprehensive Search Function! ■
* Automatic search with each keyword input. Incremental search instantly updates search results.
* Voice input is also supported for keyword input.
* Detailed keyword matching conditions can be specified, such as "prefix match" and "suffix match." Searches are instantly updated when conditions are changed.
* Full-text search is available for almost all dictionaries, allowing you to search the text of all entries.
* In-text search is available for the content of the dictionary entry you are currently reading.
* Automatically records the history of entered keywords and displayed entries. Re-entering and re-displaying is easy.

■ Sharing with Other Apps Made Possible by the App! ■
* Supports the basic Android operation "Share"! You can have the dictionary browser search text selected in another app.

* The dictionary search function allows you to freely specify the dictionary from your existing dictionary apps.

* Conversely, you can use the text of dictionary entries to perform web searches. Of course, you can also search within the dictionary app itself.


■ Customize Text for Easy Reading! ■
* You can finely adjust the font size of dictionary entry text.
* A dark theme display mode (black background + white text) is also available to reduce eye strain.
* Of course, you can also change the item size using touch controls.


■ Bookmark Important Information! ■
* You can bookmark dictionary entries at any time.

> But what about game frameworks for web games today? A wasteland. A hundred possibilities and none of them doing a particular stellar job.

This oddly reminds me of another exchange on HN, in which someone said that the state of software tooling for learning Japanese was very good - in that there are a lot of software developers interested in the problem, and therefore there are a lot of tools around that those developers have built - and the counterpoint came up that while Mandarin Chinese really has just one tool available, Pleco is significantly better than every tool that exists for Japanese. The more vibrant competition in Japanese tooling doesn't seem to have produced any benefits.

I can't pretend to have a good diagnosis of why this occurs in modern web game frameworks or in language tooling, but in the language tooling there does seem to be an issue of crowding out - a high-end Chinese-English dictionary is $20,¹² whereas LogoVista's Android edition of the Kenkyusha Green Goddess is $65³ (and if you want English-Japanese in addition to Japanese-English, that's another $65).

LogoVista's app has the UI entirely in Japanese, making it a challenge for Japanese learners. But with the dictionary costing that much, anyone thinking "I can make an English interface for this!" might well decide that licensing the dictionary will prevent them from ever being able to turn a profit.
